title: Day/night-aware TEP prior: exploiting solar-illumination independence
interpretation: The day/night-aware kernel beats the always-full-band kernel (median +1.14%, CI95 [+0.66, +1.59]). Using the notched TEP continuum at night and the full-band kernel during the day captures the best of both components.

For nighttime epochs specifically, day/night-aware vs full-band: +2.86% (CI95 [+1.66, +3.54], n=30).  The notched kernel's advantage at night (+0.00% vs notched) confirms the Step 125 finding that the TEP continuum is the active component at night.
pre_registered_prediction: The day/night-aware kernel (full-band during day, notched at night) should beat both the always-full-band and always-notched kernels.  During the day, the full-band kernel's solar tidal lines carry additional predictive information.  At night, the notched TEP continuum is the active component (Step 125: nighttime notched coherence 0.140 > daytime 0.102).  This exploits the solar-illumination independence of the TEP continuum as a predictive feature.
